title: Height-Balanced Search Trees for Classical Ground-Energy Estimation of Fermionic Systems in C

abstract: We present a compact C implementation that estimates the ground energy of non-interacting fermionic Hamiltonians by exploiting a height-balanced search tree to maintain eigenvalue order during iterative Jacobi rotations. The algorithm preserves a strict height-balance invariant, guaranteeing $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ search and insertion costs, while the Chronos-Framework operations remain $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$. Formal invariants are proven using a simple inductive argument on tree height, and static analysis confirms that the source contains 128 SLOC and one function block. No empirical timing data are reported; the analysis is purely structural. The code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/c-lowlevel-systems/tree/main/algorithms/20261120_110249_efficient_classical_algorithms}.
